title: Why Is Salvation By Faith Not By Works
paragraphs: Understanding Salvation: Faith Versus Works

The question of how a person is saved—whether by faith or by works—lies at the heart of the Christian gospel. Exploring this topic provides clarity on the nature of God's grace, the sufficiency of Christ's sacrifice, and the believer's assurance of salvation.
Scriptural Foundation: Salvation by Faith

The New Testament repeatedly affirms that salvation is a gift of God, received through faith in Jesus Christ, and not something earned by human effort or good deeds. This truth is foundational to understanding the gospel.
for by grace have ye been saved through faith; and that not of yourselves, it is the gift of God; not of works, that no man should glory. - Ephesians 2:8-9 ASV

Paul’s statement to the Ephesians underscores that salvation is entirely by God’s grace, appropriated through faith. Not only can no one boast about earning salvation, but any attempt to do so actually denies the sufficiency of God’s gift.
Why Not By Works?
If salvation could be achieved through human works, it would:
Negate the necessity of Christ’s sacrifice
Make salvation a matter of human achievement rather than divine mercy
Undermine the seriousness of sin and humanity’s need for a Savior
Paul addresses this directly in his letter to the Romans:
because by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified in his sight; for through the law cometh the knowledge of sin. - Romans 3:20 ASV
The law reveals our sinfulness, but it cannot save us. Righteousness before God is not earned, but credited through faith:
For we reckon that a man is justified by faith apart from the works of the law. - Romans 3:28 ASV
Abraham: An Example of Faith
Paul uses Abraham as a prime example of someone justified by faith, not works:
For what saith the scripture? And Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned unto him for righteousness. - Romans 4:3 ASV
Abraham’s faith—not his deeds—was counted as righteousness. This model applies to all who trust in Christ today.
Does This Mean Works Are Unimportant?
While works do not save, they are the evidence of genuine faith. True faith expresses itself in love and obedience. James addresses this balance:
Even so faith, if it have not works, is dead in itself. - James 2:17 ASV
Genuine faith results in a transformed life—a life that bears good fruit—not as the means of salvation, but as its result (Ephesians 2:10 ASV).
The Centrality of Christ

Salvation by faith alone magnifies the finished work of Christ. On the cross, Jesus declared, "It is finished" (John 19:30 ASV), signifying that He had accomplished all that was necessary for our redemption.
But now apart from the law a righteousness of God hath been manifested... even the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ unto all them that believe. - Romans 3:21-22 ASV
Assurance and Security
If salvation were based on works, assurance would be impossible, since no one could know if they had done enough. But since salvation is by faith, believers can have confidence:
These things have I written unto you, that ye may know that ye have eternal life, even unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God. - 1 John 5:13 ASV
Conclusion

Salvation by faith, not by works, is a central teaching of Scripture. It preserves the glory of God's grace, highlights the sufficiency of Christ, and gives believers assurance of eternal life. Good works naturally flow from a heart changed by faith, but they are never the means by which we are made right with God.
